why: Must_not 1 is avoided. Check 3 lists every exported function and says "a PR that only adds padLeft fails this check", so a README with no slugify section fails. Must_not 2 is broken. Check 3 decides PASS with the regex `^#+\s+'+f+'\b`, so each section must be a markdown heading whose text starts with the bare function name. A section headed "## `padLeft(s, width, fill)`" (name in backticks) or "### The padLeft function" would count as missing, even though line 3 only asks that a section exist. That is a required README layout. Check 4 also needs the summary to show `# fail 0`. That is TAP-reporter wording, and Node's spec reporter prints "ℹ fail 0" instead, so a passing `npm test` could fail the check. Line 4 only asks that npm test pass. Checks 1 and 2 test only behaviour the lines state, with no parameter-count or single-character-fill rule.
